subject.title: feat(gateway): attribute prompts to authenticated users

question: Should OpenClaw persist the currently authenticated trusted-proxy/Tailscale identifier in shared session transcripts now, before durable profile IDs and identity-management controls land?
rationale: The implementation is deliberately incremental, but it converts an authentication claim into durable, viewer-visible session metadata; that retention and disclosure boundary requires maintainer intent rather than an automated reviewer decision.

options.title: Approve the interim email-backed attribution
options.body: Confirm the existing shared-gateway trust model permits durable sender IDs now, with profile IDs replacing raw email identifiers in the planned follow-up.

options.title: Hold attribution for profiles
options.body: Defer persistence and UI labels until durable profile IDs, aliases, and display controls define the long-term identity contract.

options.title: Narrow the stored presentation
options.body: Keep attribution but store or render a constrained identity representation approved for transcript retention rather than the raw current identifier.

recommendation.title: Approve the interim email-backed attribution
recommendation.body: Confirm the existing shared-gateway trust model permits durable sender IDs now, with profile IDs replacing raw email identifiers in the planned follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: The related merged prerequisite and the open identity-program issue both identify this staged design direction.
